items.title: Why mistakes happen in radiology, and how to prevent them
items.summary: Diagnostic error written from the radiology side, which is the side he is relying on every time he accepts a report at face value.

_homepage.note: This sits next to the availability-bias and cognitive-load material already in the feed, but from the reporting end rather than the requesting end — the conditions under which a radiologist misses something are conditions an ED registrar can sometimes change by what goes in the request. Croakey is normally a health-policy source here; this is one of its clinical-safety pieces and belongs with practice rather than system news.

items.title: Only 0.7% of vinyl reissues are truly all-analog
items.summary: A database that lets you check whether a reissue's AAA claim survives contact with its actual signal chain.

_homepage.note: PressPick's first snapshot puts 0.7% of tracked reissues in the genuinely all-analog bucket, which reframes a lot of the Analogue Productions and half-speed-master coverage that already runs through this feed — including the Buena Vista Social Club 45rpm set and the Bowie half-speeds. The useful caveat the piece makes itself is that AAA is a provenance claim, not a quality guarantee; plenty of digitally-sourced pressings on the shelf sound better than their lineage suggests.

items.title: Donating Agent Skills to the Agentic AI Foundation
items.summary: The format he is already using to script his own tooling just stopped belonging to one vendor.

_homepage.note: Anthropic has handed the Agent Skills name, GitHub org and agentskills.io to the Agentic AI Foundation under the Linux Foundation — the same body that already holds MCP — with maintainers from Anthropic, Google and OpenAI serving as individuals. The practical read is that skills written now are unlikely to be stranded by one company's roadmap, and the proposed next steps include security guidance for skill authors, which matters given the malicious-skill reports circulating this month.

items.title: Devium built The Gene from half-century-old deadstock cord
items.summary: A finite run: one roll of 1970s American 6-wale corduroy found in a Midwest warehouse, and that is the whole supply.

_homepage.note: Named for Gene Clark, boxy trucker cut, two bellows chest pockets, quilted nylon lining, sewn in California with American thread, lining, labels and custom shank buttons — Devium's whole proposition is fibre-to-tag domestic sourcing, and this is the clearest test of it. Deadstock cloth means the run ends when the roll does, which puts it in the same category as the Woolrich and Pendleton pieces worth buying when seen rather than thinking about.

items.title: emDOCs Podcast 151: Orbital Cellulitis
items.summary: Brit Long's rule that labs cannot rule orbital cellulitis in or out is the kind of thing that changes a disposition decision at 3am.

_homepage.note: The practical core here is negative: normal CRP, ESR and white cell count do not exclude orbital cellulitis, and they will not separate it from preseptal disease either, so the decision stays clinical plus CT brain and orbits. Worth pairing with the trigger Long gives for reaching for the scanner — URI or dental symptoms alongside eye symptoms — because sinusitis is the usual source and that combination is common in an ED waiting room. emDocs is off the usual FOAMed list but has been the most consistently publishing of them this month.

items.title: All Hallows' Aquarium Drunkard III
items.summary: The third year of the AD writers emptying out their Halloween shelves, which is where their odder recommendations surface.

_homepage.note: The seasonal lists are the one time Aquarium Drunkard's writers abandon the house style and just name the records they actually reach for, which historically turns up library music, Italian soundtrack work and gospel oddities rather than anything new. Given the Piero Umiliani and Twin Peaks soundtrack pieces already pulled from AD this month, this is the vein the collection keeps borrowing from.

items.title: 11 PS Plus Extra game removals for November 2026 confirmed
items.summary: GTA 5 leaves the catalogue on 17 November, two days before GTA 6 arrives — a deadline, not an announcement.

_homepage.note: Eleven titles go on 17 November, with Red Dead Redemption 2 alongside GTA 5, Football Manager 26 and The Talos Principle 2. The timing is the story: Rockstar pulling GTA 5 off the subscription tier 48 hours before the sequel's 19 November launch is deliberate, and anyone part-way through either Rockstar game has three weeks to finish or buy. Push Square's removal lists are the reliable version of this; the aggregators run a day behind.

items.title: Kentmere Pan 200 – A Walk Home (A Quick Review)
items.summary: An honest first-roll account of Harman's newest budget emulsion, including the author admitting he probably underexposed it.

_homepage.note: Pan 200 is the middle child Harman added between the 100 and 400, and the consensus forming elsewhere is that it carries noticeably more midtone contrast than either. Greg May shot it in an Olympus DC 35 with a red filter and suspects he was a stop under throughout, which is more useful than a clean test — it shows what the film does when the metering is approximate. The Pan 400 five-frames piece is already in the feed, so this completes the pair.

items.title: Hands Down, Fitzroy
items.summary: The Bar Liberty and Above Board people doing southern France and northern Spain in the old Bad Frankie room.

_homepage.note: 139–141 Greeves Street, with a 40-seat parklet running down the side street — a short ride from the northside, and the pedigree is the reason to go rather than the newness: Dominic Xavier, Hayden Lambert and Manu Potoi came off Bar Liberty and Above Board, with Alex Boon from Pearl Diver behind the bar. Open from 4pm Tuesday to Saturday, so it works as an after-shift option rather than a booking.

items.title: Health of the Nation 2026: investment is improving access
items.summary: The annual census of the workforce that decides how much of the community arrives at his door instead of a GP's.

_homepage.note: Launched at Parliament House on 28 October: FTE GPs up to 30,476, training applications exceeding funded places, Commonwealth spend at $13.4 billion — and against that, a third of GPs considering retirement within five years and 72% naming rising patient complexity as the pressure. ED load is the downstream variable in all of this, so the retirement figure is the number to watch rather than the headline about improving access.
